title: The Third Eye Opens
hook: spring arrives on Shiva's mountain out of season, and Kama, the god of desire, takes aim at the god who is deep in meditation
carry: kama: an aim of life, never the master
tomorrow: how will Parvati win the god who burned desire?

segments.voice: Yesterday: the ash Daksha mocked, Shiva's devotees wear. Today closes a week.
screen: `WHAT DAKSHA MOCKED, DEVOTEES WEAR.` · `A THIRD SELECTION.`

segments.voice: On a frozen mountainside, the snow starts to melt. Out of season, trees burst into flower. Bees show up, a cuckoo sings, the breeze turns warm and sweet. Every living thing on the mountain feels it, except one. Under a tree, Shiva sits in meditation, perfectly still, eyes closed, as if spring were somebody else's business. Behind a bush, with a bow made of sugarcane and arrows tipped with flowers, crouches Kama, the god of desire. He's been sent on a mission, and he's nervous.
screen: `SPRING, OUT OF SEASON.` → `SHIVA, PERFECTLY STILL.` → `KAMA TAKES AIM.`

segments.voice: Here's why he's there. Since Sati gave up her body, Shiva has withdrawn into meditation. Sati has been born again as Parvati, the daughter of the mountain king, and she comes every day to serve him: flowers, water, a clean place to sit. He doesn't look up. Meanwhile a demon named Taraka has a boon, and in the Shiva Purana only a son of Shiva can defeat him. So the gods need Shiva to marry, and Shiva is busy being still. Indra, king of the gods, sends Kama, and Spring with him. Kama waits for his moment, Parvati standing near, and lets an arrow fly. For a moment it works. Shiva's mind stirs; he opens his eyes and looks at Parvati. Then he catches himself, looks for the cause, and sees Kama with his bow. Fire bursts from Shiva's third eye, and Kama is burned to ash on the spot. You met this at Holi, on day ninety-six; here is how the book tells it. Rati, Kama's wife, falls weeping beside the ashes, and she's promised her husband will live again. Now, what Hindus take from it is not that desire is bad. Kama, desire and pleasure, is one of the four purusharthas, the aims of a human life, alongside dharma, doing right, artha, making a living, and moksha, freedom. But Shiva is the great yogi, and many read the third eye as the eye of wisdom: desire that tries to command him burns. And Kama doesn't vanish. From then on he's called Ananga, the bodiless one, love moving everywhere unseen. Whatever wins Shiva will have to come from Parvati herself. That closes a week full of fire.
screen: `PARVATI SERVES; SHIVA IS STILL.` · `THE GODS SEND DESIRE.` · `THE THIRD EYE OPENS.` · `KAMA: ONE OF LIFE'S FOUR AIMS.` · `ANANGA, THE BODILESS.` · then, large: `AN AIM OF LIFE, NEVER THE MASTER.`

segments.voice: Sit as still as you comfortably can, and sooner or later a want will show up: to check your phone, to eat, to be somewhere else. Don't fight it or obey it; notice it, watch it rise and fall like spring around a still figure under a tree, and come back to the breath. If you pray, you can say Om Namah Shivaya, or the name of God you use, each time you come back.
The Shiva Purana. Today: Kama burned by the third eye, and living on as Ananga.
Your line: kama, an aim of life, never the master. Rati is promised her husband will live again. Seven days, kept.
